title: Short Stuff: Cellphones on Airplanes
summary: Short Stuff episode on whether cell phones can be used on airplanes. Hosts explain that the FAA and FCC ban in-flight cell phone calls: the FAA worries about interference with avionics and instrumentation, and the FCC worries about cell towers being overloaded by fast-moving aircraft handoffs and disrupting ground networks. They note airplane mode cuts cellular service while leaving WiFi on, that planes are hardened against electromagnetic interference, and that lightning and solar flares have affected instrumentation. They discuss Richard Branson's Virgin picocell service that uses the plane's WiFi for calls on some flights, the FCC's multi-year study that concluded against allowing calls (including flight attendant concerns during emergencies and passenger annoyance), and the etiquette of talking on phones in flight. Includes an unrelated personal aside about a family member's film work and a promotion for a movie podcast, which the hosts say may be edited out.

segments.title: Opening banter and cell phone ban overview
segments.summary: Hosts open with banter about a loud cell phone user on a flight, then introduce that the FAA and FCC ban cell phone calls on planes.

segments.title: History of the rules and airplane mode
segments.summary: Hosts describe early instructions to power down phones, the introduction of airplane mode, which cuts cellular service but keeps WiFi, and how in-flight WiFi changed the experience.

segments.title: Interference concerns and aircraft hardening
segments.summary: Discussion of whether phones can interfere with flight systems. Hosts say aircraft electronics are shielded, but electromagnetic interference from lightning and solar flares has affected instruments, especially GPS. No study found a crash caused by phone use.

segments.title: Break
segments.summary: Hosts announce a break before continuing.

segments.title: Etiquette and cell tower handoff problems
segments.summary: Hosts joke about passengers who ignore phone rules, then explain the FCC concern that fast-moving aircraft would overload ground cell towers through rapid handoffs, and that phones at cruising altitude generally cannot reach towers.

segments.title: Richard Branson's Virgin picocell service
segments.summary: Hosts describe Virgin offering picocell service using the plane's WiFi on some flights outside the US, and speculate it promotes Virgin Mobile.

segments.title: FCC study conclusion and passenger annoyance
segments.summary: The FCC studied the issue for years, consulted flight attendants who opposed calls especially in emergencies, and concluded against allowing them. Hosts also discuss passenger annoyance and etiquette.

segments.title: Personal aside and sign-off
segments.summary: An unrelated personal aside about a family member's film work, then the hosts sign off with the reminder to stay off your phone.
